name: Nafplio
title: Holidays in Nafplio
intro: Venetian fortresses, marble lanes and a sea-castle in the bay, in a handsome harbour town that was once the capital of Greece. Here's what Nafplio is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: View over the tiled roofs of Nafplio's old town to the little Bourtzi sea castle in the bay, framed by pink oleander and an old stone wall
facts_note: Athens airport is about two hours' drive away, so most people hire a car or take a transfer. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are the best months, warm enough for the beach with comfortable days for ancient sites. July and August are hot, often 33°C, and busy with Greek weekenders, so see the sites early. Winter is mild and quiet, and Nafplio stays lively all year as a weekend escape from Athens.

things.name: Palamidi Fortress
things.blurb: A huge Venetian fortress on the hill above town. Climb the famous stone staircase or drive up, then walk the walls for views over the bay.

things.name: Bourtzi
things.blurb: The little castle on an island in the harbour, the town's postcard view. Boats sometimes run out to it in summer.

things.name: Old town
things.blurb: Marble-paved lanes, neoclassical mansions, bougainvillea and Syntagma Square, the setting for Greece's first parliament.

things.name: Arvanitia promenade
things.blurb: A seaside path round the headland below Akronafplia, with swimming spots on the rocks and Arvanitia beach.

things.name: Ancient Epidaurus
things.blurb: The best-preserved ancient theatre in Greece, famous for its acoustics, about 30 minutes' drive away. Summer festival plays are still held there.

things.name: Mycenae
things.blurb: The hilltop citadel of Agamemnon, with the Lion Gate and royal tombs, about half an hour from town.

things.name: Karathona beach
things.blurb: A long, sandy, shallow beach a short drive or walk from town.

faqs.question: How do you get to Nafplio from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly to Athens, which has plenty of UK flights all year, then drive or take the bus, about two hours. Kalamata is another option in summer.

faqs.question: Is Nafplio worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of Greece's prettiest towns, with fortresses, good food and swimming, and some of the most famous ancient sites close by.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Nafplio?
faqs.answer: Two or three days covers the town and the fortress. Allow four to seven to add Epidaurus, Mycenae and beach days.

faqs.question: Are there beaches in Nafplio?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arvanitia is right by the old town, and the longer, sandy Karathona beach is just beyond it.
